stories.headline: Zelenskyy Announces 40-Day SBU Operation to Pressure Russia to End the War
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has approved a 40-day operation by the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) aimed at pressuring Russia to end the war. The announcement was made on June 25, following a meeting with SBU acting head Yevhenii Khmara, who reported on Ukraine's long-range and mid-range "sanctions" plans. The operation is designed to increase pressure on Russia and push Moscow towards ending its war against Ukraine. Zelenskyy announced the decision on his Telegram channel, stating that the SBU's 40-day influence operation will target the aggressor state to secure an end to the war. The move comes after a period of high-impact drone deployments by Ukrainian forces along the front lines, indicating a continued escalation of efforts to counter Russian aggression. The operation's specifics and potential impact remain to be seen.

stories.headline: Venezuela Earthquakes Live Updates: At Least 188 Dead as Rescuers Search for Survivors
stories.summary: At least 188 people have died and over 1,500 injured after two major earthquakes hit Venezuela, with the death toll expected to climb. The back-to-back quakes, which occurred just 39 seconds apart, caused widespread destruction, trapping residents beneath rubble and leaving thousands feared dead. Approximately 25,000 people are unaccounted for, with many residents taking to the streets. The US has joined the search for survivors, aiding local rescuers in their efforts. The earthquakes are considered the worst to hit Venezuela in decades, with collapsed buildings and debris scattered throughout the affected areas. Rescuers are working to locate and assist those trapped, as the full extent of the damage and loss of life continues to unfold.

stories.headline: World reacts as devastating Venezuela earthquakes kill at least 188
stories.summary: At least 188 people have died and over 1,500 injured in Venezuela after two powerful earthquakes struck the country on Wednesday. The twin earthquakes, measuring 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude, caused widespread damage, collapsing hundreds of buildings and trapping over 200 people in northern Venezuela. La Guaira was the worst-hit area, with the capital Caracas and surrounding areas also severely affected. Acting President Delcy Rodriguez declared a state of emergency, prompting global aid teams to rush to the scene. Rescue efforts are ongoing, with the death toll expected to rise as more rubble is cleared. The earthquakes have left a trail of destruction, with flattened buildings and collapsed roads reported in the affected areas.

stories.headline: Supreme court hands Trump administration big win with rulings on key immigration cases - live
stories.summary: The US Supreme Court has handed the Trump administration significant victories in several key immigration cases. The court ruled that the administration can turn back asylum seekers at the US-Mexico border, fundamentally reshaping asylum policies. Additionally, the court allowed President Trump to end temporary deportation protections for hundreds of thousands of foreign nationals from Haiti and Syria. The decisions are part of a series of immigration-related rulings issued on an emergency basis, including allowing the deportation of migrants to countries where they may face persecution. The rulings mark a major shift in immigration policy, with the court leaving open the possibility of class-action challenges to these decisions, potentially affecting thousands or millions of people. The court's term is nearing its end, with pending decisions on major cases related to presidential powers, elections, and immigration.

stories.headline: Microsoft significantly increases Xbox prices worldwide and withdraws 2TB model citing "components crisis"
stories.summary: Microsoft is increasing Xbox prices worldwide starting August 2, citing higher costs for console storage and memory due to a "components crisis." The price of 512GB models will rise by $100, while 1TB models will increase by $150. The 2TB variant will be discontinued entirely. The components crisis is partly driven by the demand for building AI data centers, an area where Microsoft has been actively involved. This price hike comes despite Xbox's recent announcement of exploring "radically different" business models to reduce console costs. The new prices will take effect on August 2, affecting Xbox sales globally. The move reflects the broader industry challenges in sourcing components, impacting Microsoft's gaming division and its pricing strategy.

stories.headline: Google Admin Enhances Agency Protections
stories.summary: Google has enhanced agency protections in its Merchant Center for Agencies, rolling out additional administration features. The updates aim to improve data protection and security for agencies managing multiple merchant accounts. This move follows recent security enhancements in Google Workspace, including new agent tools and security updates for developers. The additions also build on previous introductions, such as the three new agents in Google Security Operations, designed to hunt threats and provide context on third parties. Furthermore, Google has emphasized its commitment to AI privacy and security, ensuring that its services, including Google Workspace, maintain private, secure, and compliant AI practices. These enhancements demonstrate Google's ongoing efforts to strengthen its security and protection measures for agencies and developers. The updates are part of Google's broader strategy to safeguard user data and prevent potential threats.

stories.headline: Valve Now Claims Steam Machine Is Capable of 'Up To' 4K
stories.summary: Valve has updated the Steam Machine's store page to claim the device is capable of "up to" 4K gaming with FSR, revising its previous statement of 4K/60 fps graphics. The company has removed references to frame rate, now only stating the device can play "up to 4K." This change comes after reviews exposed performance limitations, prompting Valve to adjust its marketing. The Steam Machine's product page no longer guarantees 60 FPS at 4K resolution, instead providing a more nuanced description of its capabilities. The revision aims to manage expectations, as the device's performance has been a subject of criticism, along with its pricing. Valve's update acknowledges that 4K/60 fps graphics may not always be achievable, providing a more realistic representation of the Steam Machine's performance.

stories.headline: The Fitbit Charge 6 plunges below $90 Prime Day cuts the Fitbit Charge 6 to $85.45, bundling Google tools, GPS, health tracking, and both band sizes in the box.
stories.summary: The Fitbit Charge 6 is on sale for Amazon Prime Day, with a discounted price of $85.45, a 38% reduction from its normal price of $160. This fitness tracker features GPS, health tracking, and automatic activity detection, displaying daily steps and heart rate. It also links to compatible exercise machines to display heart rate. The Charge 6 comes with both band sizes in the box and includes Google tools. Normally priced at $159.95, the sale brings the cost down to under $90, making it a worthwhile purchase for those seeking a budget-friendly fitness tracker. This deal is part of Amazon Prime Day, which offers discounts on various products, including other Fitbit models like the Sense 2 and Versa 4, as well as Kindle and other items under $100.

stories.headline: Marco Palestra jets in for Chelsea medical as £43m transfer nears completion
stories.summary: Marco Palestra has arrived for a medical at Chelsea as the club nears completion of his £43m transfer from Atalanta. The right-back is set to sign a six-year deal with the option for Chelsea to extend it by a further year until June 2033. Inter Milan had been leading the race to sign Palestra, but Chelsea have agreed a deal with Atalanta. The transfer is expected to be finalized soon, with Palestra becoming the latest addition to the Chelsea squad. The move comes as Chelsea is also set to appoint Enzo Maresca as their new head coach, with the Italian expected to sign a five-year contract. The developments indicate a busy period of activity at Chelsea, with the club shaping its squad and coaching staff for the upcoming season.

stories.headline: Nicky Butt explains why 'people are standoffish' with Cristiano Ronaldo as he lifts lid on what ex-Man Utd team-mate is like in dressing room
stories.summary: Manchester United legend Nicky Butt shared his experience of having Cristiano Ronaldo as a teammate, stating that despite his public image, Ronaldo is personable in the dressing room. However, Butt criticized Ronaldo's current role in Portugal's World Cup squad, suggesting he is being selfish and should not be playing a crucial role at 41. Fellow former Manchester United player Paul Scholes also expressed similar sentiments, calling Ronaldo "a little bit of a problem" for Portugal. The criticism came after Portugal's 1-1 draw with DR Congo, with both Butt and Scholes questioning whether Ronaldo is still deserving of a leading role in the team. Their comments add to the scrutiny surrounding Ronaldo's position in the Portugal squad.

stories.headline: Haiti’s World Cup run ends with a Supreme Court ruling striking a blow to many fans
stories.summary: The US Supreme Court has ruled to end Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Haitians, affecting over 350,000 individuals who may lose work authorizations and face deportation. This decision comes as Haiti's World Cup run has ended, dealing a blow to fans. The ruling allows the Trump administration to terminate legal protections for migrants from Haiti and Syria who fled violence and natural disasters. Additionally, US travel bans have restricted many Haitian fans from attending the World Cup, further marred by the recent Supreme Court decision. The ruling has created uncertainty for Haitian fans and immigrants in the US, impacting their ability to work and remain in the country. The decision may lead to significant changes in the lives of thousands of Haitians living in the US.

stories.headline: MLB Trade Rumors Top 35 Trade Candidates For The 2026 Deadline We're coming up on trade season, so it's time to take our first look at the most notable players who'll likely change teams by August 3
stories.summary: The 2026 MLB trade deadline is approaching, with August 3 marking the cutoff for teams to make moves. As the season nears its midpoint, a list of the top 35 trade candidates has been released, featuring players from multiple teams. The list includes a game-changing ace and other superstar talent with varying levels of team control. These players may be on the move as teams seek reinforcements for the stretch run. The trade market is expected to be active, with teams still in the playoff picture looking to bolster their rosters. The list provides an update on the current state of the MLB trade market, highlighting potential trade candidates and possible fits for teams looking to make a push for the playoffs. The next few weeks will be crucial in determining which teams will make moves to strengthen their chances.

stories.headline: Mahesh Dixit appointed Intelligence Bureau chief
stories.summary: Mahesh Dixit, a senior Indian Police Service officer, has been appointed as the new chief of the Intelligence Bureau. He succeeds Tapan Kumar Deka, the incumbent chief of the country's internal security and counter-intelligence agency. The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, cleared Dixit's appointment. Dixit, who was serving as the Special Director of the Intelligence Bureau, will take over as the new director. The appointment was made on Thursday, with the Centre naming him as the next chief of the premier internal intelligence agency. Dixit's appointment is seen as a significant development in the country's internal security landscape. He will be responsible for overseeing the agency's operations and ensuring the country's internal security.

stories.headline: Mahesh Dixit, 1993-Batch Telangana Officer, Named Intelligence Bureau Chief
stories.summary: Mahesh Dixit, a 1993-batch IPS officer from the Telangana cadre, has been appointed as the new chief of the Intelligence Bureau. Dixit brings decades of experience in intelligence gathering and counter-terrorism operations. He previously headed the IB's Subsidiary Intelligence Bureau in Srinagar, overseeing operations in Jammu, Kashmir, and Leh during the post-Article 370 security transition. Currently serving as Special Director in the Intelligence Bureau, Dixit's appointment was approved by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet. He will serve a two-year term as Director of the Intelligence Bureau, starting upon assuming the position. Dixit's experience and expertise are expected to guide the agency's operations in the coming years. The official order for his appointment was issued on Thursday, confirming his new role as the head of the Intelligence Bureau.

stories.headline: Senior IPS officer Mahesh Dixit appointed new Intelligence Bureau chief, to succeed Tapan Deka
stories.summary: Mahesh Dixit, a 1993-batch Indian Police Service (IPS) officer, has been appointed as the new Director of the Intelligence Bureau (IB), the country's domestic intelligence agency. The Appointments Committee of the Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, approved his elevation. Dixit, currently serving as Special Director, has extensive experience, including heading the State Intelligence Bureau in Jammu and Kashmir. He will succeed Tapan Kumar Deka as the IB chief. Dixit is from the Andhra Pradesh cadre and will serve a two-year tenure. The government informed of his appointment on Thursday, with the Prime Minister-led committee clearing his name for the top post in the Intelligence Bureau. Dixit's appointment is seen as a significant development in the country's intelligence apparatus. He is set to take over as the new IB chief, overseeing the agency's operations and intelligence gathering.

stories.headline: Nihang-police standoff on Uttarakhand border during march to Dehradun
stories.summary: A standoff between Nihang Sikhs and Uttarakhand Police occurred at the Himachal Pradesh-Uttarakhand border on June 25, 2026. The group of Nihang Sikhs was marching to Dehradun and was stopped by police at the Kulhal-Vikasnagar border. The Sikhs demanded the release of four arrested Nihangs and refused to return until their demands were met. A heavy police force, including Indo-Tibetan Border Police personnel, was deployed to secure the area. The standoff lasted nearly three days before negotiations between the Uttarakhand administration and Nihang Sikhs led to an agreement. The Sikh group agreed to withdraw its march after overnight negotiations in Dehradun, bringing an end to the tense situation. The negotiations resulted in a peaceful resolution, with the Nihang Sikhs ultimately withdrawing their protest.

stories.headline: Bangladesh and China have agreed to deepen cooperation on Teesta river management and other water resources, as Prime Minister Tarique Rahman meets Chinese lead
stories.summary: Bangladesh and China have agreed to deepen cooperation on Teesta river management and other water resources. Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman met Chinese Water Resources Minister Li Guoying in Beijing, where they discussed increasing cooperation on managing Bangladesh's rivers. China has expressed willingness to assist Bangladesh in implementing the Teesta River water management project. The two countries have agreed to expand cooperation in river management, including the Teesta River Comprehensive Management and Restoration project. Chinese Ambassador to Bangladesh Yao Wen also expressed China's readiness to assist with the project. Several memoranda of understanding (MOUs) have been signed to strengthen cooperation between the two nations on this matter, following Bangladesh's 2021 initiatives. The cooperation aims to improve river management and water resources in Bangladesh.

stories.headline: Huawei and Cambricon are set to dominate China’s AI server market as geopolitics and self-reliance accelerate Nvidia’s retreat
stories.summary: Huawei and Cambricon are poised to dominate China's AI server market as the country accelerates its self-reliance efforts and Nvidia's presence retreats due to geopolitics. Cambricon's stock surged 11.6% to 1,384.93 yuan, nearing the market value of luxury liquor maker Kweichow Moutai. China has added domestic AI chips to its government procurement list, approving processors from Huawei and Cambricon. This shift is driven by the country's focus on building self-reliant hardware ecosystems for AI inference, rather than competing on foundational AI models. The Ministry of Industry and Information Technology's approval is expected to create significant demand for domestic hardware champions, reshaping global semiconductor supply chains. Huawei is now regarded as China's most promising domestic supplier of chips essential for AI development, with Cambricon also gaining prominence.

stories.headline: Multinationals remain committed to the Chinese market despite pressures, analyst says, citing the actions of Apple and Nvidia as evidence
stories.summary: Multinationals, including Apple and Nvidia, remain committed to the Chinese market despite pressures. Over 80% of Apple's 200 major suppliers have set up factories in China, highlighting the country's importance in global supply chains. China is also a significant market for Apple. Similarly, Nvidia has made notable investments in China, demonstrating the attractiveness of the market. Analysts note that few companies can afford to ignore the immense opportunities in China, with its growing demand and diversified portfolios. The actions of these companies reflect a growing consensus among global investors that Chinese assets are difficult to bypass. As a result, many US multinationals, like Tesla, continue to prioritize the Chinese market, underscoring its enduring importance in the global economy. This commitment is expected to persist despite external pressures.

stories.headline: Huawei and Cambricon lead China’s AI server chip surge, piling pressure on Nvidia
stories.summary: Huawei and Cambricon are leading China's AI server chip market, gaining ground as Nvidia's presence declines. In 2025, Chinese firms, including Huawei, captured 41% of the AI accelerator server market, with Huawei shipping around 812,000 AI chip units. Nvidia's market share decreased to 55%. Cambricon plans to triple its AI chip production in 2026, aiming to deliver 500,000 units, including 300,000 of a specific model. This surge is driven by growing demand from Chinese companies seeking domestic alternatives due to geopolitics and self-reliance efforts. As a result, China's homegrown silicon suppliers, such as Huawei and Cambricon, are filling the market gap left by Nvidia's struggles to supply the Chinese market. Domestic chip makers now claim nearly half of China's AI accelerator server market.

stories.headline: Why is market rising today? Sensex soars 800 pts, Nifty above 24,250. 3 key factors powering D-St bulls
stories.summary: Indian stock markets experienced a significant surge on Thursday, with the Sensex rising 800 points and the Nifty exceeding 24,250. Three key factors are driving the market's upward trend. The decline in oil prices is one major factor contributing to the market's gains. Additionally, the market's resilience and recovery from previous losses have also played a role. The surge in Trent shares led the gains on Wednesday, setting a positive tone for the market. The Indian stock markets, including the Sensex and Nifty, have shown notable gains, indicating a bullish trend. The market's performance is being closely watched, with investors and analysts attributing the rise to a combination of factors, including the drop in oil prices and the overall resilience of the market.

stories.headline: Stock Markets End in Green Buoyed by Falling Oil Prices and Positive Global Cues
stories.summary: Stock markets ended in the green, halting a three-day losing streak, buoyed by falling oil prices and positive global cues. Brent crude oil prices declined 1.26% to $72.81 per barrel, supporting investor sentiment. European markets rallied, with the Paris Stock Exchange gaining 1.70% and the STOXX 50 rising 2.4%. The STOXX 600 also gained 1.8% as hopes grew for a resolution to the Middle East conflict and oil prices fell below $100 per barrel. Strong buying in IT stocks and broad-based buying after Thursday's sharp fall also lifted investor sentiment. The rebound was driven by easing oil prices and positive global cues, leading to a post-lunch rebound in the Nifty and Sensex. Overall, the markets recovered from recent losses, driven by improving global market sentiment and declining oil prices.

stories.headline: Sensex closes 109 points higher, Nifty above 24,050; IndiGo, M&M among top gainers
stories.summary: Sensex closed 109 points higher at 77,100.47, and Nifty 50 climbed 34 points to 24,056. The gains were driven by strong performances from IndiGo, M&M, and Maruti Suzuki, which rose 4.8%, 4%, and 4% respectively. Other top gainers included SBI, ICICI Bank, and Kotak Mahindra Bank. However, Power Grid shares saw notable declines. The Nifty Metal index fell 1.37%, Nifty IT declined 0.86%, and Nifty Oil & Gas lost 0.87%. The broader market dipped into the red, despite the benchmark indices initially soaring over 1% in the afternoon. The modest gains came on Sensex monthly expiry day, with the indices erasing significant intraday advances to end the session with marginal gains.

stories.headline: Stock market today: Sensex, Nifty end higher, but gains remain capped; here's why
stories.summary: The BSE Sensex rose 109.25 points or 0.14% to 77,100.47, while the NSE Nifty50 index gained 34.35 points or 0.14% to close at 24,056. Earlier in the day, the Sensex had jumped nearly 800 points and the Nifty 50 had risen over 200 points, driven by declining crude oil prices and positive global market signals. However, the markets erased most of their intraday gains to end marginally higher. The surge was fueled by investor buying, with the Sensex and Nifty experiencing a significant bullish trend. Despite giving up some gains, the Indian equity indices still closed higher, with the Sensex up 0.14% and the Nifty also up 0.14%. The market capitalization increased substantially during the day due to the initial rally. The gains were capped, but the overall trend remained positive.

stories.headline: Micron Soars, Apple Sinks, and the Indexes Tread Water Micron's blowout earnings sent its stock soaring and Apple's tumbling.
stories.summary: Micron's stock surged 16% after the company reported a massive earnings beat, driven by strong demand for its memory products. In contrast, Apple's stock fell more than 6% after the company raised prices for its Mac and iPad products due to soaring memory costs. The S&P 500 index remained relatively stable despite the volatility in individual tech stocks. Micron's stock has risen nearly 270% so far in 2026, making it one of the best-performing stocks in the S&P 500 this year. The earnings report and subsequent stock movement highlight the impact of the memory boom on the tech industry, with Micron benefiting from strong demand and Apple facing increased costs. The contrasting performances of the two companies reflect the challenges and opportunities presented by the current market conditions.

stories.headline: It’s a bad time to want a new computer Apple, Microsoft, and Valve announced some difficult prices this week.
stories.summary: Apple, Microsoft, and Valve have announced price increases for their products due to soaring costs of memory and storage chips. Apple raised prices of Macs and iPads by up to $300, citing the AI industry's rapid expansion and increased demand for data center storage. The price hike affects popular products like MacBooks and iPads. Microsoft followed with an announcement to increase Xbox console prices starting August 1. The tech giants attribute the price increases to the rising costs of memory and storage chips, driven by the AI boom. The price hikes range from over $200 to $300 for some devices, indicating a new reality for consumers in the tech market. The increases are a result of the companies no longer being able to absorb the rising costs of components.

stories.headline: Alternergy sells 40% wind projects’ stake for P2.4B
stories.summary: Alternergy Holdings Corp has sold a 40% stake in its 192-MW wind projects to ABC Energy for PHP 2.4 billion. The projects include the Tanay and Alabat wind farms in the Philippines. The Philippine Competition Commission (PCC) approved the acquisition on March 11, 2026. The deal was initially announced on October 31, 2025, with A. Brown investing PHP 2.4 billion in the two wind farms. The partnership will allow Alternergy to proceed with the execution of the wind projects in collaboration with ABC Energy. The combined capacity of the wind farms is 192 MW, contributing to the Philippines' renewable energy development. The acquisition was cleared by the PCC, paving the way for the completion of the transaction and the advancement of the wind energy projects. Alternergy will retain a 60% stake in the projects.

stories.headline: Maruti Suzuki Y43, the upcoming Tata Punch rival, could launch by 2027 with SUV styling, modern features, CNG option, and attractive pricing.
stories.summary: Maruti Suzuki is developing a new micro SUV, codenamed Y43, to rival the Tata Punch and Hyundai Exter. The Y43 is expected to launch by 2027, featuring SUV styling, modern features, and a CNG option. It will be priced attractively, with an estimated starting price of ₹6.50 Lakh (ex-showroom). The vehicle will be part of Maruti Suzuki's strategy to reclaim the entry-level SUV segment. The Y43 will offer features that match premium expectations, including hybrid engine options. Maruti Suzuki is also planning to enter the electric vehicle category with the eVitara. The sub-4m SUV segment is currently booming, with several new models expected to launch by the end of 2026, making the Y43 a significant addition to the market. Its launch is anticipated to make a significant impact in the Indian automotive market.

stories.headline: Brain Drain: Google Faces Exodus of AI Talent Joining Competitors Like Anthropic
stories.summary: Google is facing a significant brain drain in its artificial intelligence sector, with several top researchers leaving to join competitors like Anthropic. Recently, Nobel Prize-winning scientist John Jumper, co-creator of AlphaFold, announced his departure to Anthropic, followed by two more prominent Google AI researchers preparing to leave. This exodus has raised concerns about Google's ability to innovate and compete in the AI space, particularly after the company failed to deliver notable innovations, lagging behind Anthropic and OpenAI. The departures have also impacted Alphabet Inc's stock, which fell 5.5% after the loss of two high-profile researchers. The talent exodus underscores the intense competition in the AI sector, with Google struggling to retain its top talent amidst a rapidly evolving landscape. The company's inability to keep pace with rivals has sparked concerns about its future in the AI race.

stories.headline: What does a $1 trillion valuation actually mean for OpenAI and Anthropic? Is AI really a productivity revolution?
stories.summary: Anthropic's valuation is approaching $1 trillion following a significant new funding round, nearly tripling its $380 billion valuation from February 2026. This surpasses OpenAI's valuation of $852 billion. Anthropic's annualized revenue is $39 billion, compared to OpenAI's $25 billion. On secondary markets, Anthropic's implied valuation has crossed $1 trillion, exceeding OpenAI's by over $100 billion. The rapid growth of these AI companies is unprecedented, with some predicting that the value of AI companies will eventually exceed that of non-AI companies. The funding and valuation increases reflect the growing interest and investment in artificial intelligence, with companies like Anthropic and OpenAI leading the charge in the development and application of AI technology. Their revenue growth is the fastest seen in human history, with OpenAI's revenue reaching $10 billion.

stories.headline: Mind Games: Talent wars heat up as AI startups take on Big Tech
stories.summary: A talent war is intensifying in the AI sector, with tech giants like Google losing researchers to rivals OpenAI and Anthropic. This exodus has impacted Google's market value, highlighting the competition for top AI minds. Anthropic is gaining ground, poaching top engineers from OpenAI and DeepMind. Companies are scrambling to retain elite AI researchers with high pay and strict noncompetes. The talent war is rewriting the rules in Silicon Valley, where bold founders once drove innovation with independence. Now, new-age AI founders are signing up for lucrative paychecks, driving the competition for AI talent. The battle for top researchers is fierce, with companies offering sky-high pay to attract and retain the best minds in the AI sector. This trend is expected to continue as the demand for AI expertise grows.

stories.headline: After Anthropic shutdown, China's Z.ai closes frontier gap as it plans dual listing
stories.summary: China's Z.ai is planning a dual listing in Shanghai to fund its pursuit of artificial general intelligence (AGI). The company aims to improve its models to achieve the upper bound of intelligence, following the success of its GLM-5 model. Z.ai's GLM-5.2 model has gained attention for its performance in coding, reasoning, and agentic workflows, nearing top US AI performance. The move comes after the US government shut down global access to Anthropic's most powerful AI models, sparking a global scramble for sovereign AI. Z.ai's new technology is seen as a cost-effective alternative, with its open-source model gaining traction. The company's plans to list domestically are fueled by strong investor interest, as China seeks to close the gap in AI technology. Z.ai's ambitions are driven by its goal to achieve AGI, with the listing proceeds expected to fund its research and development efforts.
